title: Grocery theme — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Cash & Carry. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. (No image generation this session, so the build is code-led; cards carry facts, not comps.)

options.label: Cash & Carry
options.lineage: warehouse-club floors: stacked crates, pallet stickers, per-kilo price signage
options.thesis: The shop as a working warehouse floor — goods at quantity, prices as big printed signage, unit price first-class; refuses the clean white produce-app grammar.
options.viewport: A signage masthead over a crate-strip of category tiles; below, the offer row as stacked price boards — huge stencil price, small unit price on its rail tag, quick-add stepper molded into each crate cell. The merchant's primary is the crate plastic; their photos sit in the crates.
options.risk: Industrial grammar can read discount-hard; the food must stay appetizing inside the cells, and a premium deli merchant may find it blunt.

raised.raise: States print themselves: SALE, OUT OF STOCK, ADDED, empty and error are pallet stickers in the label grammar — never a floating toast or chrome badge.
One shared clock: a single motion timing system — everything lands like one stamp, no scattered hover effects.
Choreographed pairing: the hero offer is image and price block answering each other across a seam at poster scale, never a slapped banner.
Total line commitment: one hardware line weight carried through every control, so the crate line is a system, not a garnish.
Designed attention: focus and hover are designed shelf-light states, not default outlines.
Charged quiet: the dense grid earns deliberate empty bands — the floor breathes between pallets.

options.label: The Weekly Flyer
options.lineage: the supermarket circular every household reads
options.thesis: The storefront as this week's flyer: saturated price blocks, starburst offers, dense product grid with slashed prices — promotion as the native language.
options.viewport: A flyer front page: masthead with the week, one lead offer at half-page scale, then the deal grid — every cell a price block with product photo, big price, crossed-out original.
options.risk: The most familiar promotional grammar in the category — closest to what grocery e-commerce already gestures at; familiarity is the trade.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The shop as a typed transcript on curved glass.
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript; products print as lines.
options.case: A text transcript buries image-led food shopping; grocery shoppers do not identify with a machine room.
options.kept: States print themselves — no floating chrome.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.thesis: The catalog as an editable pattern buffer on one clock.
options.viewport: A code buffer whose cursor line is the downbeat.
options.case: Shoppers restocking groceries do not identify with live coding; the buffer obscures products and prices.
options.kept: One shared clock for all motion.

options.label: Brodovitch Spread
options.thesis: Shopping as paired spreads — pose and answer across a gutter.
options.viewport: A two-page spread, image left, headline right.
options.case: Sparse luxury editorial fights a medium–high-density grocer; spreads hide the catalog.
options.kept: Choreographed image/price pairing in the hero.

options.label: Menhera Sheet
options.lineage: pastel character sheet with hardware accessories
options.thesis: The shop as a candy-pink motif sheet with a mascot.
options.viewport: A centered mascot inside a repeating motif border.
options.case: A mascot sheet cannot carry a multi-merchant grocery catalog; audience and clarity both fail.
options.kept: Total commitment to one line weight everywhere.

options.label: Alien Understory
options.thesis: Browsing as proximity-lit paths through glowing growths.
options.viewport: A dark field where labels bloom on approach.
options.case: A dark proximity-reveal field hides stock, prices and the task; nobody buys rice by torchlight.
options.kept: Focus and hover as designed light states.

options.label: Ikebana Alcove
options.thesis: One product arranged; the emptiness does the selling.
options.viewport: An off-center arrangement in charged empty space.
options.case: Low-density contemplation against a medium–high-density working shop; the errand loses.
options.kept: Deliberate quiet bands pacing the dense grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean grocery app grammar — white ground, fresh green accent, rounded cards, photography carousel — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Rounded header, hero carousel, category chips, 4-col card grid with green add buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every grocery app, by design.
